title: Polaronic Response of a Supersonic Impurity Strongly Coupled to a Bose Condensate
authors: Sooshin Kim, Yoonsoo Kim, Seokmin Jang, Jee Woo Park
abstract: How a mobile impurity exchanges momentum and energy with a many-body environment is a central question in nonequilibrium quantum physics. This exchange becomes particularly complex when the impurity moves rapidly and is strongly coupled to its bath. Here, we realize an interaction-tunable cold-atom collider with fermionic $^{40}$K impurities immersed in a $^{23}$Na Bose--Einstein condensate. A species-selective Raman pulse simultaneously launches the condensate and quenches the interspecies scattering length, producing an initial relative speed 36 times the condensate speed of sound. We track the ensuing relative motion as the interspecies interaction is tuned from weak coupling to resonance. At weak and intermediate coupling, the impurity dynamics are well described by a finite-energy two-body collision model. Near resonance, however, the early-time impurity acceleration is markedly suppressed relative to the two-body prediction, corresponding to a strong enhancement of the apparent dynamical inertia. The enhancement is observed near two distinct Feshbach resonances. These observations provide evidence for a polaronic response in the strongly coupled, supersonic regime of a degenerate Bose--Fermi mixture.
summary: This research explores the complex momentum and energy exchange between a rapidly moving impurity and a Bose-Einstein condensate. By tuning interactions near Feshbach resonances, the authors observed that the impurity's response deviates significantly from simple two-body predictions. This deviation signals a polaronic enhancement of the impurity's effective mass in the strongly coupled, supersonic regime.
main_problem: The study investigates how a mobile impurity exchanges momentum and energy with a many-body environment, especially when moving rapidly (supersonically) and strongly coupled to the bath.
main_result: Near resonance, the impurity exhibits a marked enhancement of its apparent dynamical inertia, providing evidence for a polaronic response in the strongly coupled, supersonic regime.
method: The study combines experimental measurements of impurity velocity evolution with theoretical modeling based on two-body collision approximations and Bogoliubov theory.
model_or_system: The system is a cold-atom collider consisting of fermionic $^{40}	ext{K}$ impurities immersed in a $^{23}	ext{Na}$ Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC). The interactions are tuned using Feshbach resonances to explore varying coupling strengths.
key_observables: Impurity velocity $v_I(t_1)$, apparent dynamical inertia ($1/s$), and momentum transfer signatures.
important_parameters: Supersonic relative speed ($\approx 36$ times the speed of sound), interaction strength ($a_\uparrow$), and proximity to Feshbach resonances.
main_assumptions: The weak coupling regime is modeled by a finite-energy two-body collision model, and the strong coupling regime is analyzed by interpreting deviations from this model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental sequence, the reconstruction of impurity velocity vs. time, and plots comparing the measured drag response to the theoretical two-body collision model, showing the divergence near resonance.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem, details the experimental setup using cold atoms, develops theoretical models for drag force in different coupling regimes, presents measurements showing agreement with simple models at weak coupling, and finally highlights the deviation near resonance as evidence for polaronic dressing.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum gases, specifically the crossover between simple collision dynamics and strongly correlated, dressed quasiparticle behavior (polarons) in a supersonic regime.
